sentences.text: It took Austria 155 days to get a government. Why?
Who can vote? Austrian citizens from 16, at home or abroad.
That leaves out nearly one in five residents over 16.
You cross one party, and can also back up to three of its candidates.
Seats are shared out by votes, but a party needs 4% to get in.
MPs sit in the National Council, which makes the laws and can vote the government out.
The Federal Council, sent by the nine states, can mostly only delay laws.
In 2024, the Freedom Party came first with 29%, far from a majority.
Two rounds of talks failed, then three other parties teamed up under Chancellor Christian Stocker.
And the President? Elected by the people for six years, with a run-off if needed. Alexander Van der Bellen appoints the Chancellor, and can even dismiss the government.
Should people who live in Austria but aren't citizens get a vote?
